header: The languages of one circular check each other (step 40a, made trilingual in step 42a). A circular of this plant comes in English and Hindi, and sometimes in Bengali too: the pages say the same thing with the same numbers and dates. OCR reads each page on its own, so a number that stands on two pages is read twice, independently. I use that as a second reading: it is free, offline, and works on the text already stored. When one page has a number that another page has a little differently (seen: `20-0802` on the Hindi page and `20-08-2026` on the English page; `(215,000)` for `(Rs 15,000)`, the rupee sign read as a 2), at least one reading is wrong. What is found. I put pages in a GROUP when they are in different scripts (English, Hindi, Bengali) and have the same important numbers (at least 2 in common and at least half of their union). A group holds 2 or 3 pages: English + Hindi, English + Bengali, English + Hindi + Bengali (Hindi and Bengali pages join through the English page when they do not share enough numbers with each other). In a group:
- a number that stands on this page AND on another page of the group is CONFIRMED (two independent readings);

- a number on this page only that is a little different (one or two digits) from a number another page has and this page lacks is a DISAGREEMENT: one page against one (`20.0802` on the Hindi page, `20.08.2026` on the English page), or one page against two that agree with each other;
- a number on this page only that is a longer form of a number this page has elsewhere and another page confirms is a VARIANT (`215000` next to `15000`: a stray digit in front);
- any other number on one page only is a SINGLE: I conclude nothing about it.

What is recorded (the checks of the answer card's gate, circularAnswer.ts, which REFUSES an answer whose value holds an unconfirmed number): the confirmed numbers of each page, and as UNCONFIRMED only the readings the evidence points at: both sides of a disagreement between one page and one other page (at least one of them is wrong and nothing says which), the lone page when two pages agree against it, and a variant. My rule is that an honest "not found" is better than a confident wrong answer, so I trust neither side by its language (English-page OCR does read numbers far better than Hindi or Bengali OCR: in the first archive report almost all the garbage was on the Indic pages; set TRUST_ENGLISH to true to keep a lone English reading in a one-against-one disagreement). A second reading that confirms a number lifts it again (combineChecks). I never mark a single: a number that stands on one page only is often right. This file is pure; crossCheck.selftest.ts unit-tests it.

symbols.name: LANGUAGE
symbols.sig: const LANGUAGE: Record<string, string> = { latin: "English", devanagari: "Hindi", bengali: "Bengali" }

symbols.name: scriptOf
doc: Gives the script a page is mainly written in: "mixed" when neither the Indic scripts nor Latin dominate, "none" when there is too little text to say.

symbols.name: majorNumbers
doc: I take the important numbers of a page to be those with 4 or more digits, or with a point, and I write each in one canonical form. What a second reader wrote in [handwritten: ...] is not part of the page.

symbols.name: isNoise
doc: I do not conclude anything about a number like this when it stands on one page only: a clause number (2.3, 4.91) or a bare year of our time (written 2025 on one page and JAN-25 on the other).

symbols.name: editDistance
symbols.sig: function editDistance(a: string, b: string): number
doc: Edit distance between two digit strings: one step is an insert, a delete or a change of one digit.

symbols.name: TRUST_ENGLISH
doc: My rule is an honest "not found" over a confident wrong answer, so this is false: in a disagreement between one page and one other page, both readings are unconfirmed. Set it to true and an English reading is kept.

members.name: a
doc: The page whose number differs from a number that the other pages have.

members.name: b
doc: One of the pages that have the other number.

members.name: support
doc: Counts the pages that have the other number (1: page against page; 2: page against two that agree).

members.name: base
doc: The number that this one is a longer form of.

members.name: languages
doc: e.g. "English + Hindi + Bengali".

members.name: confirmed
doc: Per page, I keep its important numbers that stand on another page of the group too.

symbols.name: groupPages
doc: Here I join pages with the same important numbers in different scripts into groups (a page joins through any page it matches).

symbols.name: isLongerForm
doc: `215000` counts as a longer form of `15000`: the same digits with one to three stray digits in front.

symbols.name: crossCheck
doc: I cross-check every group of pages of one circular here.

symbols.name: titleFamily
doc: I strip the language tag ("(Eng)", "(Hin)", "(Beng)", "- Hindi" ...) from a title, make it lower case and flatten punctuation and spacing: the circulars of one family end up with the same one. "" when nothing is left.

symbols.name: siblingsOf
symbols.sig: export function siblingsOf(circulars: { id: number; headline: string }[]): Map<number, number[]>
doc: For each circular, this gives the ids of the OTHER circulars of its family (the same title apart from the language tag). I leave out a circular that has none.

symbols.name: WitnessPage
doc: A page of ANOTHER circular, brought in to check this one.

symbols.name: witnessPage
doc: The page number a witness page has inside a group: from WITNESS_BASE up, so it never clashes with a circular's own pages, which are below it.

symbols.name: decodeWitness
symbols.sig: export function decodeWitness(page: number): { circular: number; page: number } | null

symbols.name: crossCheckWithWitnesses
symbols.sig: export function crossCheckWithWitnesses(own: PageText[], witnesses: WitnessPage[]): Group[]
doc: Cross-checks the pages of ONE circular with the pages of its family as witnesses. I return only the groups that hold a page of this circular.

symbols.name: twinChecks
symbols.sig: export function twinChecks(groups: Group[], keep: (page: number) => boolean = () => true): NewCheck[]
doc: Here I record per page the confirmed numbers, and as unconfirmed only a non-English side of a disagreement and a non-English variant.

symbols.name: twinChecksFor
symbols.sig: export function twinChecksFor(chunks: { page: number | null; index: number; text: string }[]): NewCheck[]

params.name: chunks
params.type: { page: number | null; index: number; text: string }[]

doc: The twin checks of a circular from its stored chunks (the same input as checkRowsFor).

symbols.name: combineChecks
symbols.sig: export function combineChecks(second: NewCheck[], twin: NewCheck[]): NewCheck[]
doc: I merge two sets of checks of the same circular (the second reading's and the twin checks; then those and the rupee-slot checks) into one: a page's confirmed numbers are those either set confirmed, and a number is unconfirmed only if neither confirmed it. The reader of the second set is added to the reader name.

symbols.name: mergeIntoStored
symbols.sig: export function mergeIntoStored(existing: StoredCheck | null, twin: NewCheck, textHash: string): NewCheckRow
doc: For the archive: I merge a twin check into what is already stored for the page. A stored check about OTHER text (its fingerprint differs) is replaced, never kept.

symbols.name: pageScripts
symbols.sig: export function pageScripts(pages: PageText[]): { page: number; script: Script }[]
doc: The script of each page of a circular, grouped or not, for the report: I want to see whether there are Bengali pages at all, and whether they found a twin.

members.name: scripts
doc: The script of each page (optional: the report shows the counts when it is given).

members.name: siblings
doc: The other circulars of its family (the same title in another language), when it has any.

members.name: rupee
members.type: { page: number; suspects: Suspect[]; junk: JunkSlot[] }[]
doc: Per page, the amounts with a stray leading digit (currency.ts attachedDigitSuspects) and the symbols before amounts (rupeeSlotJunk).

symbols.name: ownedBy
symbols.sig: const ownedBy = (item: CircularFindings, g: Group, present: Set<number>) =>
doc: Counts over a whole archive, and what recording the twin checks would do. I list and count a group with pages of several circulars (a family) once: under the lowest circular it touches that is IN the report (a run restricted with --ids has only some of them).

symbols.name: SCRIPT_NAME
symbols.sig: const SCRIPT_NAME: Record<string, string> = { latin: "English", devanagari: "Hindi", bengali: "Bengali", mixed: "mixed", none: "too little text" }

symbols.name: pagesByScriptLine
symbols.sig: export function pagesByScriptLine(m: Map<string, { total: number; grouped: number }>): string
doc: "English 61 (in a group: 21), Hindi 40 (21), Bengali 0, mixed 3, too little text 2".

symbols.name: pageName
symbols.sig: const pageName = (item: CircularFindings, g: Group, page: number) =>
doc: "page 1", or, in a group with pages of several circulars, "circular 85 page 1". I never show a witness page number: it is internal.

symbols.name: whereIn
doc: "Hindi page 1", or "Hindi circular 85 page 1".

symbols.name: renderReport
doc: I write the report as Markdown: the readings that disagree or look garbled first (they are what gets recorded as unconfirmed), then the numbers on one page only.
